[engine] A memory-pressure counter is not a measurement of the resource the engine depends on. `Pages free` moves with page-cache size (large cache -> low free -> FAST) and with other-process footprint (large anon -> low free -> SLOW) in opposite directions, and reporting their sum averages the two into a number that predicts nothing.

<!-- generated by harness_engine/build_memories.py from traces/lessons.jsonl -->
<!-- lesson_id: eng-mh-0015 | class: measurement-hygiene | superseded_by: - -->

**class**: `measurement-hygiene`

## 為什麼（because）

Tested on prefill250 pp2048 @ -ub 6144: five independent processes gave 286.67 / 173.54 / 155.62 / 166.06 / 166.63 t/s with rho(usable%, t/s) = -0.70 -- the run with the LEAST free memory was the only one to clear 250. The instrument had recorded `free + inactive`; measured in the same session, free was 5.94 GiB while the actual page cache (File-backed pages) was only 3.33 GiB and anonymous was 3.82 GiB. Re-run with the page cache recorded explicitly and FORCED up 4.3x on three of six runs (2.32 -> 9.96 GiB, free driven to 0.06 GiB): rho(cache, t/s) = +0.09, and the whole batch landed on the same 155-184 band. So the correct variable was found and it also does not explain the spread.
